question: Why do first-time workspace admins abandon setup before inviting their team?

evidence.text: I got to the roles screen and realised I didn't know who should be an owner versus an admin. I closed the tab and meant to come back.
My manager signed us up and told me to set it up, but I can't approve a paid plan, so I stopped once it asked about billing.
We needed SSO before anyone else could log in, and that is an IT ticket. That took three weeks.
Setup took longer than I expected.
Didn't have time this month, it was end of quarter.
The roles part was fine. The import from our old tool failed twice and I gave up.
62% of abandoned setups stop on the roles and permissions step; median time on that step is 4m10s.
Abandonment is 1.4x higher for workspaces created in the last two weeks of a quarter.
How do I give someone admin rights without giving them billing access?
Once finance approved it a month later I finished setup in an afternoon.

interpretations.statement: Admins stall because the roles and permissions model is hard to map onto their organisation.
interpretations.mechanism: The role model forces an org-design decision the admin was not expecting to make alone.
assumptions: The roles step is where people stop, not merely where they pause.
interpretations.discriminator: Abandonment drops when the roles step is deferred or pre-filled with defaults.

interpretations.statement: The person running setup lacks authority to commit, so setup waits on someone else's approval.
interpretations.mechanism: Setup is delegated to someone without budget or identity authority; the stall is an approval queue.
assumptions: Abandoned workspaces often resume after an approval elsewhere.
interpretations.discriminator: Abandoners more often lack billing permission, and resumed setups follow a billing or SSO change.

interpretations.statement: Setup collides with end-of-quarter workload; the stall is about timing, not the product.
interpretations.mechanism: Trials started near quarter end compete with closing work and are dropped for lack of time.
assumptions: Quarter timing is not confounded with company size or plan type.
interpretations.discriminator: The quarter-end effect holds within the same company size and plan.
